# .github/: CI, deploy and the Targets workflow

Notes for anyone editing `workflows/ci.yml` or `workflows/targets.yml`, or reading their results. What every contributor must know (CI is the authority, generated files belong to CI) is in the root `AGENTS.md`.

- **One native installer:** CI calls `sudo bash tools/environment/install-native.sh`, also used by the portable agent Dockerfile. Update its package list when changing CI tools; do not duplicate installation commands in the workflow. `npm run setup`, `doctor` and `env` are documented in `tools/environment/README.md`.
- **Native CI toolchain:** Ubuntu 24.04 with gcc 13, clang 22 (apt.llvm.org) + `libclang-rt-22-dev`, lldb 22 and `llvm-22` (its `llvm-symbolizer` makes clang's ASan reports readable), gdb 15, valgrind 3.22, Node ≥22, FFmpeg. Stored targets: macOS arm64 and ubuntu-24.04-arm (all samples), windows-latest (`platform` samples). The `project-runner` job in `targets.yml` runs `check.mjs` (`make test` on the starter and solution zips of each entry in its matrix: today the Mario and Credit projects; the `tools/check/fixtures/caesar` fixture, whose memory check runs the real `leaks` on macOS and whose leaky variant must fail it; and the LT exercise `m03-doctor`, whose entry sets `exercise:` because its codes name the exercise id) on macos-14 and ubuntu-24.04-arm. On PRs it also runs when a path in the `pull_request` filter of `targets.yml` changes (`tools/check` except `*.md`, `tools/ci/verify-project-run.ts`, `src/testing`, the Mario and Credit project folders, all of `content/modules/m03-going-native/`, and `targets.yml` itself). Windows is not run (WSL only).
- **Reference environment.** Unless the change is docs-only (see the next note), the `check` job logs the runner image (`ImageOS`, `ImageVersion`) and the versions of gcc-13, clang-22, lldb-22, gdb, valgrind, node and ffmpeg; the `deploy` job installs nothing and logs nothing. We select the gcc major version by package name (`gcc-13`) and accept patch drift in clang 22 (apt.llvm.org) and the other apt tools. `verify --check` ignores version strings (`generatedBy`, each target's `compiler`) and compares behaviour only, so drift cannot turn it red.
- **CI-owned generated files.** On a same-repo PR that is not docs-only, the `check` job runs `npm run verify` with a read-only token. If `src/generated/{samples,traces,sessions}` changes in behaviour, it uploads the files, fails on purpose, and the separate `commit-generated` job (the only one with `contents: write` and `actions: write`; it runs none of the PR's build or test code, only `tools/ci/unpack-generated.mjs`, which accepts nothing but regular files strictly under `src/generated/{samples,traces,sessions}/`) commits them as `github-actions[bot]` to the PR branch and dispatches CI for the new head (a push made with `GITHUB_TOKEN` triggers no workflow, `workflow_dispatch` is exempt). The checks on the final head SHA come from the dispatched run. If the branch moved meanwhile, the bot skips the push and your own push gets its own run. Fork PRs cannot be pushed to and just fail `verify --check`. Timed-out runs are never cached (`cacheRuns` in `tools/verify/cache.ts`). Native sessions (`src/generated/sessions/<module>.json`, `docs/adr/0005-native-sessions.md`) go through the same flow; the macOS runs inside them come from `src/generated/targets/` (Targets on `main`), not from this bot. Observed on the #89 probe (#98): the bot's push also showed `pull_request` runs of CI and Targets at the new head, by `github-actions[bot]`, that stayed `action_required` and then read `failure`. Judge the head by the dispatched (`workflow_dispatch`) run. A probe session needs its module to pass `lint:content`, which requires `module.yaml` with a non-empty `lessons` list. `src/generated/sessions/` is untracked until a module on the branch has a session, and `git add` of a missing path exits 128 under `bash -e`, so `commit-generated` adds that folder only when it exists (a samples-only artifact once failed there, review of #97).
- **Build variables.** The `Build` step passes the repository variable `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables) as `VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, the public OAuth client id for Drive sync (`src/progress/AGENTS.md`). Unset, the build hides the feature. It is a variable, not a secret: the id ships in the page anyway.
- **Docs-only pull requests.** The `changes` job runs `tools/ci/docs-only.mjs` on the merge commit's diff (`HEAD^1..HEAD`, `fetch-depth: 2`). If every changed file is the root `README.md` or `PLAN.md`, an `AGENTS.md` in any folder outside `content/modules/` (the app bundles Markdown from exercise and project folders), a skill's `SKILL.md` or `.claude/skills/` link, `LICENSE` or under `research/`, `check` skips the native toolchain install, version log, verify, trace, exercises, videos, animations, typecheck, `npm test`, build, e2e and the WebM transcode, and runs only `lint:content` and `vitest run tools/docs tools/ci` (the agent-notes and classifier tests that `npm test` would run). `check` still reports, so a required status never hangs (a trigger-level `paths-ignore` would leave it pending). Pushes, manual and bot-dispatched runs always run everything, so `deploy` is unchanged. It is an allowlist, not `**/*.md`: tooling reads Markdown under `content/` and `tools/`. `CLAUDE.md` is not on it because the repo forbids that file. Add a path only if no tool or test reads it.
- **`targets.yml` on PRs.** `gh pr checks`/`gh run list` show its runs under the workflow name `Targets`; only `project-runner` runs on a PR (the sample job is skipped). The `targets` concurrency group is per-ref for PRs so a PR run never queues behind `main`. Apple clang on `macos-14` is 15.0 and `make` is 3.81, so keep Makefiles 3.81-safe.
- **Native sessions on macOS.** On `macos-arm64-appleclang`, `--target-run` also runs every session (`steps.all` and `steps.macos`) and writes `<module>.sessions.json`, which the commit job stores beside the samples; `verify` shows it only while its hash matches the session folder. A session problem there is a `::warning::` annotation recorded in the file, never a failed step, so it cannot block the macOS sample results. `npm run dod`'s `macos-sessions` row is where a missing, stale or broken macOS run fails (`tools/verify/macos-sessions.ts`); it is red on a stack branch until Targets has run on `main`. The dispatch-only fixture step runs with `--strict-sessions`, so an unstable fixture session fails it. A manual dispatch also runs the `m97` fixture sessions and uploads them as the `sessions-fixture-<target>` artifact (nothing is committed).
